s1.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic chest pain with exertion
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Substernal chest pain lasting less than 5 minutes
Chest pain occurs with running more than 2 miles
Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
High exercise capacity on treadmill test
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

shortlist.label: Coronary Artery Disease
shortlist.why_kept: 3-vessel involvement on CCTA and severe ischemia on PET-MPI

shortlist.label: Stable Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with exertion and ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

shortlist.label: Unstable Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Severe ischemia on PET-MPI and high-risk coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Severe ischemia on PET-MPI and 3-vessel involvement on CCTA

shortlist.label: Microvascular Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with exertion and evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of substernal chest pain with exertion, high LDL, and evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI, along with 3-vessel involvement on CCTA, are most consistent with coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Stable Angina
rejected.why: While the patient has exertional chest pain, the presence of ST depressions during recovery and severe ischemia on PET-MPI suggest a more complex disease process than stable angina alone.

rejected.label: Unstable Angina
rejected.why: The patient's chest pain is described as lasting less than 5 minutes and occurring with a specific trigger (running more than 2 miles), which does not fully align with the typical presentation of unstable angina.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of persistent chest pain or elevated troponins, which are key features of acute coronary syndrome.

rejected.label: Microvascular Angina
rejected.why: The patient has evidence of epicardial coronary disease on CCTA and coronary angiogram, making microvascular angina less likely as the primary diagnosis.
